Title: November 2026 Core Update & Gemini 4 Hydrogen Explained | Zorvex Technologies
Description: Google’s November 2026 core update has finished and Gemini 4 Hydrogen now powers AI Mode. Here’s what changed and what to check in Search Console.

Home / Blog / AI SEO

# Google’s November 2026 Core Update and Gemini 4 Hydrogen: What Changed in Search

Google’s November 2026 core update has finished and Gemini 4 Hydrogen now powers AI Mode. Here’s what changed and what to check in Search Console.

By the Zorvex Technologies team

If your traffic jumped around in November, you’re not imagining it. Google ran a broad core update, switched AI Mode to a new model, and a Search Console bug made AI visibility look worse than it really was for a few days. Here’s what happened, in plain terms, and how to read your numbers without panicking.

## The November 2026 core update is complete

Google started rolling out the November 2026 core update on 10 November and said it could take up to two weeks. It finished on 24 November, after 14 days. Google has also said a December 2026 core update is coming, with a focus on complex queries and personalisation.

A core update isn’t aimed at any one kind of site or trick. Google simply changes how it weighs quality across everything it has indexed, so some pages climb and others slip, even if nobody touched them.

Our advice: give it at least a week after the rollout ends before you judge anything. Google says the same, so a fair comparison starts around 1 December. Put a full week after the update next to a full week before it began (ending 9 November), and look at individual pages and queries, not just the total.

## Gemini 4 Hydrogen now runs AI Mode

On 12 November Google made Gemini 4 Hydrogen the default model in AI Mode for all users worldwide. Google says it’s also used for the hardest questions in AI Overviews, and Google’s own Search post called it the biggest model upgrade to Search yet.

Why should you care? If you track how often AI Mode or AI Overviews cite your pages, November's numbers now cover two different models. So if your citations changed around 12 November, it may be the new model, not anything you did.

## A Search Console bug undercounted AI impressions

A logging error undercounted AI impressions in Search Console’s generative AI report from 9 to 11 November. Google says the error affected data logging only, so a dip on those days is missing data, not lost visibility. When a similar bug hit in August, Google restored the data a few days later, so these numbers may jump back up.

The bug overlaps the first day of the core update, which makes it easy to misread. A sharp drop on 9–11 November is very unlikely to be a penalty.

## AI Overviews are getting more personal

On 23 November Google said AI Overviews and AI Mode will start tailoring some answers to each person’s recent searches. That means the answer your rank tracker sees may not be the one your customer sees. Treat AI visibility tools as a useful sample, not a single “true” ranking.

## Your checklist for December

- Annotate 10 November (update start), 12 November (Hydrogen) and 24 November (update end) in your reports.

- Exclude 9–11 November when you compare AI impressions in Search Console.

- Compare winners and losers by page type (service pages, blog posts, location pages) to see what Google now rewards.

- Improve pages that dropped with clearer answers, original data and expert input, rather than chasing quick fixes.

- Expect more movement: a December core update is already announced.

Not sure how the update affected you? Send us your site. We’ll do a free SEO check and show you which pages moved, and what we think caused it.

Title: How AI Overviews & AI Mode Choose Sources (2026) | Zorvex Technologies
Description: Google published a guide on how AI Overviews and AI Mode pick and link sources. Here’s what it says and how to make your pages eligible to be cited.

Home / Blog / AI SEO

# How Google’s AI Overviews and AI Mode Choose Their Sources

Google published a guide on how AI Overviews and AI Mode pick and link sources. Here’s what it says and how to make your pages eligible to be cited.

By the Zorvex Technologies team

On 24 November 2026 Google published a new Search Central page, Attribution and factuality in Search generative AI features. It explains how AI Overviews and AI Mode pick the pages they link to. Google says nothing has changed; it’s just describing how things already work. Even so, it’s the clearest explanation we’ve had from Google, so it’s worth a read. Here’s our summary.

## 1. It starts with normal search rankings

AI Overviews and AI Mode start from the top normal search results and use their snippets to build the answer. So if your page doesn’t rank well in regular search, it’s unlikely to be cited. Good rankings are still the way in.

## 2. “Query fan-out” widens the net

The model often runs extra, related searches to gather more material. Ask “best CRM for a small plumbing business” and it may also look up pricing, integrations and reviews. Pages that answer those follow-up questions clearly get more chances to be used.

## 3. Answers are checked against other sources

Google says it checks cited pages against other top results, data feeds and its Knowledge Graph. Claims that agree with other trusted sources are safer to cite. So it helps to keep your facts accurate and the same everywhere: your site, your Google Business Profile and your directory listings.

## 4. Some topics are held back

Safety and policy checks can stop an AI answer from showing at all, especially for sensitive “Your Money or Your Life” topics or breaking news with little coverage.

## 5. You must be indexed and snippet-eligible

Only pages that are indexed and eligible to show a snippet in Search can appear as supporting links. If you block snippets with nosnippet or your page isn’t indexed, it can’t be cited.

## 6. Don’t fake freshness

One more thing: Google says not to change a page’s date unless the content has really changed. Bumping the date without real edits won’t help.

## What this means for your SEO

- Keep doing the fundamentals. Technical health, indexing and strong rankings feed directly into AI citations.

- Cover the follow-up questions. Add FAQs, comparisons and pricing details that match likely fan-out searches.

- Write extractable answers. Put a clear, direct answer near the top of each section.

- Keep facts consistent across your website, Google Business Profile and listings.

- Check your snippet settings so you’re not accidentally opting out.

Google also says “optimising for generative AI search is optimising for the search experience, and thus still SEO.” We couldn’t agree more. Showing up in AI answers comes from good SEO, not a separate trick. If you’d like a hand with that, see our SEO services.

## Sources

- Google AI Mode Tracker 2026 (24 Nov entry) — Keywords Everywhere

- Generative engine optimization — Wikipedia

- AI Mode vs AI Overviews: How to Measure the Merge — The HOTH

Title: GEO 2026: How to Get Cited by ChatGPT, Gemini & Perplexity | Zorvex Technologies
Description: Generative Engine Optimization explained with 2026 research: what earns AI citations in ChatGPT, Gemini and Perplexity, and how to measure it.

Home / Blog / GEO

# GEO in 2026: What Gets Your Pages Cited by ChatGPT, Gemini and Perplexity

Generative Engine Optimization explained with 2026 research: what earns AI citations in ChatGPT, Gemini and Perplexity, and how to measure it.

By the Zorvex Technologies team

Generative Engine Optimization (GEO) simply means getting your content mentioned in the answers that tools like ChatGPT, Gemini, Perplexity and Google AI Mode give. You’ll also hear it called AEO, LLMO or just AI SEO. The term started in a 2023 research paper; in 2026 it’s part of every sensible SEO plan. So what actually gets a page cited? Here’s what the latest research says.

## What the 2026 research says

### The best paragraph matters most

A study published in October 2026 looked at 158,099 AI answers with 468,037 citations across commercial questions. One consistent finding: pages with a strong, directly relevant paragraph got cited more on every engine tested. The lift was about 9.5% on ChatGPT, 7.8% on Gemini and 4.8% on Perplexity.

The engines also behave differently. A title that matches the question was linked to more citations on Gemini (about +17%) and Perplexity (about +5%), but made almost no difference on ChatGPT. In other words, there’s no single “AI” to optimise for.

### A small share of pages wins most citations

Peec AI analysed 30 million sources cited across ChatGPT, Google AI Mode, Gemini, Perplexity and AI Overviews. On ChatGPT, the 31% of URLs cited most often took 59% of all citations. List-style pages performed especially well: 52% of listicles on ChatGPT reached a high citation rate, even though they were under a fifth of cited URLs.

### Be careful with “share of citations” dashboards

A 2026 research survey found that, in one setup, 57.8% of repeated ChatGPT prompts didn’t search the web at all. If a tool only counts answers that include citations, it can make your visibility look better than it is. The authors suggest measuring across several engines, prompts and time periods, rather than trusting one “cited by ChatGPT” score.

## New ways to see AI traffic

OpenAI opened its Business Hub in beta on 10 November 2026. Verified businesses can track ChatGPT mentions and click-throughs. Meanwhile, one study found 79.2% of 28,500 sites got at least one AI referral in September 2026, but for most of them AI visits were still small next to organic search.

## A practical GEO checklist

- Lead each section with a clear answer in 2–3 sentences, then add detail.

- Match the question in your headings (“How much does a sport court cost?”), which helps on Gemini and Perplexity.

- Publish comparison and “best of” content where it genuinely helps buyers, with honest pros and cons.

- Add original facts: prices, timelines, data from your own projects. Unique facts are worth citing.

- Keep ranking in Google. AI Mode and AI Overviews start from top search results.

- Track several engines and many prompts over time, and claim your ChatGPT Business Hub listing.

We have a specialist on the team who focuses on AI search. If you’re curious how your business shows up in ChatGPT or Gemini, ask us for a free AI visibility check.

# Ads in Google AI Mode: Multiturn Ads, Up to Four Ads and 10 New Countries Including India

Google now shows ads on AI Mode follow-up questions and has expanded AI Mode ads to India, Australia and more. Here’s how to get your campaigns ready.

By the Zorvex Technologies team

AI Mode is Google's chat-style search, and it's getting more ads. Three changes from the last month are worth knowing about if you run Google Ads.

## 1. Multiturn ads: ads on follow-up questions

On 28 October 2026 Google announced multiturn ads in the US. They let ads appear on the follow-up questions people ask during an AI Mode conversation, not just the first search. Search Engine Roundtable confirmed they were live in early November, with “Sponsored” ads showing on the third and fourth follow-ups too.

Follow-up questions tend to be the most specific and the closest to buying (“which one is cheapest?”, “who installs this near me?”). That makes these ad spots valuable.

The good news: you don’t need a new campaign type. Google uses your existing Search, Shopping and Performance Max campaigns. Exact and phrase match can show on the first question; broad match, AI Max, Shopping and Performance Max can show on the first question and the follow-ups.

## 2. Up to four ads per AI Mode answer

By early November, AI Mode was showing up to four ads on a single response. Google says click-through rates are already similar between sponsored and organic product listings inside AI Mode.

## 3. AI Mode ads expand to 10 more countries

Also on 28 October, Google expanded AI Mode ads to Australia, Canada, India, Kenya, Malaysia, New Zealand, Nigeria, Pakistan, the Philippines and Singapore. Google says AI Mode queries are on average three times longer than traditional searches.

Multiturn ads are still US-only for now, and Google hasn’t said when they’ll reach other countries.

## The catch: limited reporting

The downside is reporting. AI Mode results are mixed into your normal campaign and search terms reports, and right now there’s no way to tell a click on a follow-up question from a click on the first one.

## How to get ready

- Test broad match or AI Max on proven campaigns, with strong negative keyword lists.

- Write assets that answer comparison and pricing questions, since these match follow-up queries.

- Clean up your Merchant Center feed with detailed titles and attributes for Shopping and PMax.

- Review search terms weekly, because longer, conversational queries will appear.

- Use value-based bidding so Google bids more for the leads and sales that matter most.

Want your campaigns ready for AI Mode? Take a look at our PPC services, or book a free ads audit and we’ll tell you what we’d change.

# Google Ads Updates, November 2026: AI Max Tracking, 7-Day Smart Bidding Learning and More

The Google Ads changes that matter this month: AI Max click tracking, the 7-day Smart Bidding learning limit, PMax income exclusions, purchase badges and more.

By the Zorvex Technologies team

Google Ads changed a lot this autumn, and most of it you can safely ignore. These are the eight changes we think matter for small and mid-sized advertisers, with what we'd actually do about each one.

## 1. You can now identify AI Max traffic

AI Max can show your Search ads on queries beyond your keyword list. Google has now documented a ValueTrack parameter, {search_term_matchtype}, that helps separate normal keyword clicks, AI Max broad expansions and keywordless matches in your click data.

What to do: add it to your tracking template. Then you can compare AI Max clicks with your normal keyword clicks in GA4 or your CRM, and see whether the extra reach is worth paying for.

## 2. Smart Bidding “Learning” now lasts 7 days at most

Google rewrote its help page as About Smart Bidding learning. It now says the Learning status never lasts more than 7 days, down from the 7–14 days often quoted before. Performance Max and Demand Gen campaigns may need up to 7 days to ramp up serving.

What to do: don’t keep changing targets within one conversion cycle, and judge results after the ramp-up, not in the middle of it.

## 3. Household income exclusions in Performance Max

Performance Max campaigns now support campaign-level household income exclusions across all placements, a control advertisers have asked for.

## 4. Attributed Branded Searches

Launched on 3 November, this free measurement tool shows how many people searched for your brand on Google or YouTube after seeing your Demand Gen or YouTube video ads. Find it under Goals > Summary > Consideration.

## 5. Purchase volume badges on Shopping ads

Eligible Shopping ads can now automatically show recent sales figures to build trust, as long as you report item-level conversions.

## 6. Merchant Center “Ads opportunities” for agencies

Agencies can now spot products with no ad coverage, or very little traffic, across several Merchant Center accounts from one dashboard.

## 7. Invalid traffic overview card

A new card in Google Ads shows how much you were credited back for invalid (fake) clicks.

## 8. Google backs dynamic conversion values

Google Ads Liaison Ginny Marvin said that feeding dynamic, predicted conversion values into Smart Bidding is a proper part of value-based bidding, not a workaround. So if some leads are worth far more to you than others, tell Google.

## Our top three actions for December

- Add AI Max tracking and review its search terms weekly.

- Set up conversion values (even estimated ones) so Smart Bidding chases profit, not just volume.

- Check your Attributed Branded Searches if you run YouTube or Demand Gen.

Want help putting any of this into practice? Have a look at our Google Ads management, or ask us for a free audit of your account.
